title: fix(tui): BUG-0072 tool-call-pre hash seam + TUI stderr guard
body:
Closes the BUG-0072 registry entry (TUI frame corruption). Report: `.planning/bugs/BUG-0072-tui-frame-corruption-hook-error-stderr-leak/BUG_REPORT.md`.

### Root cause (two layers)
1. **Latent since #8858**: scheduler dispatches `tool-call-pre` with a `tool-pre-hook-payload` struct; `gsd-tool-guard` does `(hash-ref payload 'tool-name #f)` → contract violation on **every** scheduler tool call (hook-pass fallback let tools run; the guard was a silent no-op for 7 weeks).
2. **BUG-0068 Wave B trigger**: hook errors escalated `log-debug` → `log-error`; the default logger's stderr pump (which holds fd 2 from process start and ignores `current-error-port` parameterization) painted the exception + backtrace into the TUI frame mid-redraw → stale `[SYS]` fragments, character-interleaved rows, exception text in the prompt area.

### Fix
- **Seam (Layer 1)**: `tools/scheduler-execution.rkt` now dispatches a hash `(hasheq 'tool-name … 'tool-arguments … 'tool-call-id …)`; struct remains internal plumbing.
- **TUI stderr guard (Layer 2)**: new `tui/stderr-guard.rkt` — swaps `current-logger` to an unparented `'q-tui` logger at TUI init (default pump never sees runtime error records), surfaces each error-level record to the status line + a spill file, restores the original logger on both teardown paths. Wired in `tui/tui-init.rkt`.
- Guard regains function: executing-mode planning-artifact writes are blocked again (new test proves `'block` through the real key names).

### Tests
- New: `tests/test-tui-stderr-guard.rkt` (4/4 — logger swap, callback+spill surfacing, pump isolation, restore idempotence)
- Seam regression: `tests/test-hooks-complete.rkt` 30/30 (payload must be a hash with the exact keys)

1. **Projection drift is already tolerated** (status header, `## Last Failure`, PLAN index status are excluded from snapshot hashes). 2. **Hook exception swallow**: hook errors went to `log-debug` only; critical-hook block messages omitted the exception — `/go` failures were undiagnosable without `-W debug`.
3. **register-shortcuts contract violation**: `wiring/extension-setup.rkt` dispatches with a plain payload and no ctx, but gsd-planning / github-integration / racket-tooling handlers used the ctx-based `ext-register-command!` API → `ctx-command-registry: contract violation` on every TUI start, silently swallowed; slash commands never reached the palette.

## BUG-0068 secondary finding 2: verifier chokes on markdown-decorated Verify criteria

**Live blocker on the v1.00.29 campaign**: every delivery verification of a v1.00.29 wave died deterministically with


— W0 at 14:26 (recorded in its doc's Last-Failure), then both W1 verification jobs (21:17, 23:59, log `gsd-verification-vj-2-…`). The campaign could not complete W1.

Wave documents (per the v1.00.29 planning bundle) declare Verify criteria as **markdown prose bullets**:

title: BUG-0069: surface campaign auto-retry in the TUI + honest error hints

## BUG-0069: campaign auto-retry was invisible — and the error hint lied about it

**Reported live** (2026-09-10, v1.00.29 campaign, executor session `V8CFZB5N` → `VXMB369Z`): after provider retries exhausted (`[retry: attempt 5/5]` → `[ERR] Network error contacting api.z.ai …`), the transcript's last line read **"[SYS] Error persisted after 5 retries. Type /retry to resubmit."** — while the campaign's infra-retry lane had actually resubmitted the wave automatically. The session resumed; the user had no way to know, and the advice on screen was wrong.

### Root cause (two defects, one fix)
1. `gsd.campaign.infra-retry` was emitted by the coordinator (fast lane BUG-0024-W3, slow lane BUG-0067) but had **no TUI reducer** — every automatic re-attempt was invisible.
2. `format-error-hint` is context-blind: during a campaign, a failed turn *will* be re-attempted automatically, so "Type /retry to resubmit" is false advice.

- `tui/state-events/core-handlers.rkt`: new `gsd.campaign.infra-retry` reducer → `[SYS] [wave N] infra failure — fast-lane auto-retry in 30s / slow-lane retry in 480s (6720s patience left); attempt not consumed, resuming automatically`
- `tui/state-events/helpers.rkt`: `format-error-hint` gains `#:campaign-active?` — during a campaign the hint states the automatic re-attempt ("no /retry needed"); **non-campaign hints stay byte-for-byte identical**
- `runtime/gsd-query.rkt`: `current-gsd-campaign-active-query` seam (A1-03 pattern), wired in `tui-init.rkt` from `current-gsd-campaign-owner`'s dynamic extent
- `infra-retry-policy.rkt` / `go-orchestrator.rkt`: slow-lane event now carries remaining patience

title: BUG-0067: patient slow-lane infra auto-resume + settings wiring + IPC render fix
body:
## BUG-0067 (#9652): campaign infra-retry exhausts into a manual /retry on sustained provider outages — patient auto-resume with increasing delay

**Evidence (v1.00.29 launch day, campaign `6ae3ac51`):** three api.z.ai bursts in one afternoon; two exhausted the fast budget (3 × 30/60/120s ≈ 3.5 min patience) and stopped the campaign — each stop costing a manual `/retry`. Provider probes between bursts: 10/10 clean (bursty outage — exactly the class that outlasts the fast budget). Full analysis: `.planning/bugs/BUG-0067-infra-retry-budget-exhaustion-requires-manual-resume/BUG_REPORT.md`.

### Fix

**Slow lane (patient auto-resume):** when the fast budget exhausts on an infra-class failure, the coordinator keeps re-attempting the same wave with backoff that keeps **doubling** past the fast lane's 120s cap (240/480/900/900…, capped at `gsd.campaign-infra-max-delay`), until the total patience horizon (`gsd.campaign-infra-patience`, default 7200s) is consumed. Attempt is **never consumed** in either lane. Patience `0` restores the legacy fail-closed stop **byte-for-byte**. Waits are chunked (15s default) with a durable-cancellation check per chunk — a `/stop` persisted mid-backoff ends the wait within one chunk and surfaces `campaign cancelled during infra-retry backoff`.

**Settings wiring (BUG-0044 class):** `gsd.campaign-infra-retries` was documented in policy.rkt since v1.00.22 but never read by any accessor. Now wired through `settings-query.rkt` + the `settings.rkt` facade, consumed at the go-orchestrator composition root via `resolve-effective-infra-retry-policy` (keyword override > settings key > canonical default; invalid values warn-and-default — a typo'd settings file can never crash a campaign mid-wave). New keys: `gsd.campaign-infra-patience`, `gsd-campaign-infra-max-delay`.

**IPC render gap:** worker-emitted `gsd.wave.outcome-error` events cross the JSON IPC boundary with **string** keys; the TUI's keyword-only `hash-ref` rendered every such stop as `wave outcome: unknown` (the confusing line in the incident transcripts). An all-string-keyed payload is now normalized to symbol keys, so infra stops render `[infra-failed]` + the resume instruction.

### Files

- `extensions/gsd/policy.rkt` — 4 new parameters (patience, max-delay, slow-delay shape, wait-chunk)
- `extensions/gsd/infra-retry-policy.rkt` — slow-lane seams: backoff shape, patience ledger, stop messages (legacy prefix preserved), resolver, slow-state, phase-keyed telemetry (`fast`/`slow`)
- `extensions/gsd/go-orchestrator.rkt` — composition root + slow-lane arm (chunked cancellation-aware wait); budget/patience are per-`/go`-invocation, documented
- `runtime/settings-query.rkt`, `runtime/settings.rkt` — three accessors, never-crash semantics
- `tui/state-events/core-handlers.rkt` — IPC payload normalization
- `docs/architecture/parameter-inventory.rktd` — +4 audited parameters

- `tests/test-gsd-campaign-infra-retry.rkt`: slow-lane auto-resume integration (1 fast + N slow runs, message accounting, attempt preserved), `/stop`-during-backoff prompt cancellation; exhaustion-path tests pin `patience 0` for the legacy contract (documented flip)

body:
## fix(release): purge restored workspace bytecode in the release test job (BUG-0065 root cause)

**Root cause of all three identical release-lane failures** (cohort-report `[ASSERTION_FAILURE]` 122 passed / 5 failed, every final-claim verdict collapsed to `unverified`):

The release `test` job runs in the **prepared-env restore lane**, which skips setup-racket's `Clean stale q workspace bytecode` step (it is gated on `prepared-env.outcome != 'success'`). The restored snapshot's `.zo` files carry **mtimes newer than the fresh checkout**, so Racket's mtime invalidation trusts them and executes the **producer's bytecode instead of the checked-out sources**.

**Proof (from the run-34237587725 artifact):** the executed suite name is `final-claim verdict cohort (c3, v1.00.27 w5)` — **lowercase** — a W5-development-era source string that does not exist anywhere in the tagged tree (`tests/test-ci-cohort-report.rkt:1488` reads uppercase `(C3, v~a W5)`). CI ran old bytecode, whose rows/guard semantics predate the final W5 iteration, against the current module expectations → 5 unverified verdicts, deterministically (3/3 runs).

Local reproduction matched the mechanism exactly: editing the test file (content change → test `.zo` recompiled) over a stale module `cohort-report_rkt.zo` (mtime trusted) reproduced the exact 5 failures; purging both caches fixed it (25/25). 500/500 standalone runs passed with fully fresh caches.

### Changes

- **release.yml** `test` job: new `Purge restored workspace bytecode` step (same find as setup-racket's purge, preserving the frozen `tests/metadata-discovery/fixture`) before the fast suite — **the lane tests exactly what it checked out**.
- **tests/test-ci-cohort-report.rkt**: permanent BUG-0065 diagnostic dump — the fully-guarded gate state (per-row verdict/satisfied/reasons + guard-evidence keys) lands in per-file output on every run, so any recurrence is diagnosable from the artifact.
- **tests/test-release-workflow-contract.rkt**: contract pins the purge step and the diagnostics so neither can regress.

### Supersedes

## BUG-0062 (#9596): GSD events never reached TUI reducers

`apply-event-to-state` dispatched reducers via a raw hash lookup on `(event-ev evt)`, but the registry is keyed by **strings** while every live GSD emitter passes **symbols** (`emit-gsd-event! TEST shape (string ev):   status-message: "W0 verifying — budget 1800s · log …"

## BUG-0058 — coordinator-owned GSD verification is invisible in the TUI

Closes #9584.

After a wave executor returns its final response, `/go` runs the declared Verify command in the coordinator-owned verification lane, but the TUI kept displaying the executor summary. A healthy multi-minute gate looked like a hang, encouraging operators to interrupt valid verification (observed live during v1.00.24 W4: 380 s gate, durable campaign advanced, TUI unchanged).

### Fix (visibility-only; verifier ownership/timeout/cancellation semantics unchanged)

title: fix: bounded same-wave verification repair with exact diagnostics (#9583)
body:
## BUG-0060 — verification failure gets no repair retry

Closes #9583.

### Problem
When the coordinator's declared Verify chain rejected a delivered wave, `run-campaign-wave` persisted `failed` and stopped the campaign with no same-wave repair attempt. The verifier's command/exit/log diagnostics never reached a successor executor, and the delivered worktree/branch evidence was at risk on the failure path.

### Fix (bounded, at-least-once, fail-closed)
- **Classification**: only an owned declared-Verify subprocess failure (evidence pair `("verify" #f "cmd=... exit=... log=...")`) is repairable. Boolean/blank verdicts and repository/branch/evidence failures stay terminal.
- **Budget**: new `current-gsd-wave-verification-repair-retries` (default `1`), independent from no-change and infra retry budgets. Each repair consumes a fresh fenced attempt (`begin-attempt!`), preserving D5 at-least-once semantics.
- **Work preserved**: the repair attempt continues on the SAME branch/worktree via `call-with-retained-wave-worktree!` (new in wave-executor.rkt); every attempt still records a truthful artifact-ledger entry. A no-progress guard stops repair when the branch head is unchanged.
- **Exact diagnostics**: the delivery verifier's failing evidence now embeds a bounded `failed-output-summary` (last 4 KiB of combined output), and `verification-repair-context-block` carries the verifier message verbatim into the successor prompt with an explicit "rerun the COMPLETE declared Verify chain" completion rule.
- **Fail-closed exhaustion**: budget exhaustion or no branch progress emits `gsd.verification.repair-exhausted` (new event; `repair-started` on retry) and produces a truthful terminal `wave-failed` with the verifier reason.
- **Size discipline (BUG-0042)**: `wave-outcome-reporting.rkt` extracted from `go-orchestrator.rkt`; file 1499 → 1497 lines, 24 → 22 defines; `go-orchestrator-baseline.rktd` re-recorded in the same commit per the fixture's maintenance contract.

title: chore(deps): bump actions/download-artifact from 7 to 8
body:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 7 to 8.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

title: fix(gsd): BUG-0037 W2 — hook dropped tool arguments; all bash calls collapsed into one signature
body:
Fourth live false-kill exposed the **actual root cause** — the watchdog never saw tool arguments at all.

## Root cause
1. `step-executor.rkt` built post-tool-result hook messages with only `'content` and `'name`. The stall signature (name + arguments digest) therefore degenerated to `"bash|"` for **every** bash call — each kill fired at exactly the hard limit with "repeating 'bash'", whatever the limit was (3 → 8 → 15). Threshold tuning was treating symptoms.
2. `wave-executor.rkt` also truncated argument values at 64 chars, collapsing distinct long commands that share the `cd /home/user/src/q-agent/q && ` prefix.

## Fix
- Hook messages now carry `'arguments` (from `tool-call-arguments`).
- Signature digest is full-fidelity: canonicalized `~s` of the complete argument set; string-form arguments (provider JSON-parse fallback) digest by content; missing arguments keep the documented degenerate `""` digest (defensive: truly identical-looking calls still steer/kill).
- New LIVE REGRESSION tests: 25 distinct commands sharing a cd-prefix never trip; 20 distinct string-form arguments never trip; missing-arguments repeats pin the defensive contract.

## Verification
Fast suite 1141/1141 green; both stall suites pass; pre-commit 18/18.

body:
Third live-campaign false-kill fix. The 5/8/20 thresholds from PR #9536 still killed legitimate exploration: the W2 executor was hard-killed at 8 calls for repeating similar greps between other work.

- Auto-retry classification (PR #9536) confirmed working: the killed attempt spawned a fresh session automatically — the thresholds were the remaining issue.

title: fix(gsd): BUG-0037 — repetition-based mutation-stall watchdog v2
body:
BUG-0037 (v1.00.20 W1): the mutation-stall watchdog now detects REPETITION within a recent window instead of counting all mutation-free calls, and watchdog deaths are retryable infrastructure instead of terminal campaign stops.

## Root cause
The v1.00.17 watchdog tripped on a flat 60-mutation-free-call budget. Orchestration-scale waves legitimately need 60+ DISTINCT reads before their first edit — the v1.00.19 campaign's W5 was killed twice by exactly this, classified as terminal `wave-failed`, halting the campaign both times.

## Changes
- **wave-executor.rkt** — v2 watchdog: call signature = tool name + normalized args hash; sliding window of 10; soft steer at 2 identical signatures (latched once), hard kill at 3; absolute backstop at 200 for signature-cycling livelocks (INFO log at 75%); a mutation resets the counter AND clears the window; kill snapshot carries `stall-reason` / `stall-tool` / `recent-tools` so messages tell operators what looped.
- **go-orchestrator.rkt** — observe-hook records now carry `'arguments` (without them every read collapsed to one signature — any 3 reads would trip); `gsd-stall-exn` maps to a retryable `'infra-failed` outcome at BOTH conversion sites, so bounded auto-retry resumes with prior-attempt context; hard-failure message names the looped tool + recent distinct tools.
- **tests** — W0 characterization pins flipped into v2 regression tests (70 distinct reads never trip; identical triple kills; window aging/backstop/inert opt-outs); legacy watchdog suite rewritten to v2 semantics.

With isolation ON (v1.00.17 default since W8), per-attempt worktrees invalidate the tool worker's captured allowed-roots (`current-allowed-roots` = cwd at worker start, never refreshed — sandbox/worker-tools.rkt:50). Every edit/write is rejected for BOTH the main checkout and the executor's own fresh worktree; executors fall back to raw shell/python mutation that bypasses Racket-aware guards. Observed live in the v1.00.18 campaign within two waves.

This PR rolls the default to OFF (the proven legacy shared-checkout path used successfully by v1.00.16 and v1.00.17 waves) until worker allowed-roots track worktree lifecycle properly. `#:isolate? #t` remains the explicit opt-in. Test expectations flipped accordingly; full report: `.planning/bugs/BUG-0028-worktree-worker-stale-allowed-roots/BUG_REPORT.md` (includes secondary defect S1: the `gsd.worktree-isolation` settings key was declared but never wired).

title: fix(BUG-0021): decode chunked-transfer bodies on pooled connections (SSE corruption)
body:
## Summary

Fixes **BUG-0021** — the "model makes typos / cannot execute correct commands" report on deepseek-v4-flash.

### Root cause

`pool-send-request!` (W2, #9507) returned the **raw socket** for `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` responses. With `networking.pool.enabled=true`, every streaming SSE body therefore carried raw chunk framing: at each TCP write boundary a `<hex-size>\r\n…\r\n` sequence landed **inside** SSE data lines. When a chunk border split a JSON tool-call argument mid-token, characters were dropped/mangled (`"path: "` missing quotes, `/q-agentplanning`, `.plan/waves`) — exactly the reported "typos". The legacy path was unaffected because `net/http-client` auto-decodes chunked bodies.

The W3 bake missed it: short single-shot replies fit inside the first chunk; corruption scales with response length.

### Mitigation already applied

`networking.pool.enabled=false` everywhere (VPS + local) before this fix; flag-off is byte-for-byte legacy.

### Fix

- NEW `make-chunked-input-port`: RFC 7230 chunked decoding wrapper — hex size lines (incl. chunk extensions), chunk data, per-chunk CRLF, terminating 0-chunk + trailers. Consuming the terminator marks the pooled entry **reusable**; EOF-mid-chunk or malformed boundary faults it.
- Chunked branch of `pool-send-request!` returns the decoding wrapper.
- Regression tests: mock server emits 7-byte chunks splitting a `data:` line mid-token → asserts byte-identical logical body, clean SSE/JSON parse (`path` intact), and reuse-after-clean-termination. (The mock initially forgot the mandatory post-chunk CRLF and the decoder rightly faulted — test validates the fault path too.)

## Test plan
- [x] tests/test-conn-pool.rkt 10/10 (incl. 2 new BUG-0021 cases)
- [x] openai-compatible / stream-peer-close / midstream-stall / sse-phase-timeout-bounds / auto-retry / request-network-policy: 165 passed
- [x] scripts/pre-commit.rkt: All checks passed

## Summary

Fixes **BUG-0020**: every `/go` campaign died at spawn with

```
campaign runner failed: inherit-coordinator-runtime-config: contract violation
  expected: (or/c hash? #f)
  given: #<session-config>
  at: runtime/session/executor-inheritance.rkt:16:24
```

**Fix:** widen the contract to `(or/c hash? session-config? #f)`. No behavior change — the normalization path existed all along.

**Regression test:** `BUG-0020` case in `tests/test-executor-inheritance.rkt` covers struct-with-override (inherits provider+model) and struct-without-override (untouched).
